entry.title: Why I Needed a Safe Way to Inspect QR Codes on iOS (and the Tool That Solved It)
entry.summary: QR codes have quietly become one of the easiest ways to deliver malicious links. They show up in phishing kits, physical social‑engineering attempts, fake parking meters, restaurant menus, and even printed scam flyers. If you work in cybersecurity or DFIR, you’ve probably run into situations where you need to inspect a QR code without opening it. The problem? A colleague of mine built QR Lume, a small iOS utility designed specifically for this problem. It lets you safely inspect the raw contents of a QR code inside Apple’s sandbox, with zero telemetry and no third‑party tracking. 🔍 What it does Runs fully inside Apple’s native sandbox Makes no external requests unless you choose to Contains no analytics, no tracking, no third‑party SDKs Supports scanning from camera or photo library Includes a hex + string viewer for deeper inspection 🛡️ Why this matters DFIR triage Mobile security testing Investigating suspicious physical QR codes Teaching junior analysts safe inspection workflows Privacy‑minded users who want to see what they’re scanning 📱 The app QR Lume on the App Store Would love feedback from anyone working in mobile security, DFIR, or privacy. What features would make a tool like this even more useful in your workflow?

entry.title: Screenshot Diffing: Pixel-Level Comparison Techniques
entry.summary: Screenshot diffing compares two images of the same page to detect visual changes. The four main approaches are pixel-by-pixel comparison (fast, brittle), perceptual hashing (fast, misses subtle changes), structural similarity index (models human perception, best balance), and AI-based diffing (handles dynamic content, expensive). The right choice depends on your tolerance for false positives and your budget. You have two screenshots: one from before a code change, one from after. You need an algorithm that answers: "Did the UI change in a way a human would notice?" That's harder than it sounds. entry.title: Movie Buddy
entry.summary: This is a submission for the OpenClaw Writing Challenge Long-time lurker and reader of posts in the DEV community and wanted to finally try my hand at one of these challenges while I am stuck at home with laryngitis. After a lot of searching my daily life for something that I can streamline or get some assistance. After no success, I resulted to finding a movie to watch and made a mental note to record a review/rating on Letterboxd; not that I think that my opinion matters but I like to keep track of what I watched, what I thought, and how my view stacks up against the rest of moviegoers. I figured out that I could set up a little chatbot that can talk to me about the latest movies that I am watching or have just watched. Talking with it through Telegram like I would friends walking out of a the movie theater. It is currently set up to scrape reviews to figure out what pros and cons are for the movie not just what the movie scores on a scale of 1 to 5 stars. This also helps me expand on what I am writing by asking me questions about if I agree with this pro or this con people are saying about the movie. I am glad to have tried this and hope to create/share more tools using this fun platform.
